title: The perfect way to end Comic Con weekend is attending Lost Boys
transcript: Hello from round 29. Got one last Lost Boys in before I head south tonight. It was a really fun one because it was right after the last day of New York Comic Con, so you could tell there was a lot of people seeing the show for the first time that had seen the movie before. And usually how I tell if there's a movie heavy, heavy audience is if the leaden into superpower gets a bigger reaction than the leaden into reckoning, which was absolutely the case tonight. I also loved how many kids were in the audience tonight. I think Lost Boys is a great show for kids. Maybe not like Super Young, but like that 7 to 12 range. Absolutely. I often get asked what are the good family shows on Broadway right now. And of course there's the obvious all of the Disney shows. Definitely Paddington when that opens up next year. But like, Lost Boys really doesn't have anything super inappropriate for those older children. It does get a little intense, a little scary at times, but I think this is actually more appropriate than the original 80s film is because there isn't that five minute long useless sex scene for no reason. And because you have the character of Sam and the Frog brothers. They bring in this humour that really connects with kids. And you could tell that tonight based off of all like the children laughing at scenes like the dinner scene in the show I also think that because at the core of this show, it really is the simple premise of good versus evil it doesn't get as dark as similar shows like the outsiders, which I think is is much more for teens that it is for young kids. Tone wise, The Lost Boys the stage musical is closer in tone to a film like The Goonies that does again get a little darker than it is to the original Lost Boys film. Just because of the way that they've edited this for the stage and the way that the musical version comes across. Though do be aware there is, of course, gore in the musical, but it, it feels minimal, and especially if you're sitting further back, it feels very theatrical. It doesn't look like it's real at all. This is absolutely the kind of show that 10 year old me would have absolutely fallen in love with. I, I mean, me now has fallen in love with it, but absolutely when I was a kid, I would have eaten this up. Really super fun show tonight for my last show in New York for a couple of weeks and for Pierre's last show as David on this week of Ali's vacation. So really great show. Can't wait to be back at the end of the month.
classificationReason: Creator attended 'round 29' at the Palace right after New York Comic Con, describes audience composition and shares opinions on the show's family-friendliness. Clear first-hand review.
